question: What factor(s) distinguish the people aboard the Titanic who survived from those who did not?
answer: Gender (women ~73% vs men ~21%); class (1st ~62% down to crew ~24%); age is a weaker factor.
SQL: SELECT Gender, AVG(CASE WHEN Survived THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS rate FROM titanic GROUP BY Gender; SELECT Class, AVG(CASE WHEN Survived THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS rate FROM titanic GROUP BY Class; SELECT CAST(Age / 10 AS INTEGER) * 10 AS age_bin, AVG(CASE WHEN Survived THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS rate FROM titanic GROUP BY age_bin;

question: How did the relationship between income and life expectancy change between 1950 and 2025?
answer: Life expectancy rose at every income level; the whole cloud shifts up and to the right; the poor-rich gap narrowed.
SQL: SELECT year, quartile, AVG(life_expectancy) AS mean_le FROM (SELECT year, life_expectancy, NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY income) AS quartile FROM gapminder WHERE year IN (1950, 2025) AND income IS NOT NULL AND life_expectancy IS NOT NULL) t GROUP BY year, quartile ORDER BY year, quartile;

question: Build charts and describe the characteristics of eight-cylinder cars relative to other cylinder counts in this dataset.
answer: Lowest fuel efficiency; highest horsepower and weight; almost all USA-origin.
SQL: SELECT Cylinders, AVG(Miles_per_Gallon), AVG(Horsepower), AVG(Weight_in_lbs), COUNT(*) FROM cars GROUP BY Cylinders; SELECT Cylinders, Origin, COUNT(*) FROM cars GROUP BY Cylinders, Origin ORDER BY Cylinders, Origin;
